sources.citation: Mortensen, Christian J. 2021. The Kemaloh Lun Bawang language of Borneo. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (ScholarSpace handle 10125/75955).
sources.quote: 'in many of the modern Dayic dialects, stress appears to be predominantly final, especially in those such as the Sa'ban varieties (cf., e.g., Clayre (1992); Blust (1999)) and the dialects of the upper Padi River ... which have undergone series of dramatic sound changes evidently triggered by strong word-final stress.' Secondary (cites Clayre 1992 and Blust's SEALS IX paper).
sources.note: Most recent Dayic (Kelabit-Lun Dayeh) grammar with a stress chapter (3.4, incl. acoustic correlates for Lun Bawang) and a subclassification chapter covering Sa'ban; p.52 restates Sa'ban final stress. Secondary for Sa'ban.
